resources.string: * EXPERIMENTAL: talks to OpenMANET Comms / ATAK Vx talk groups. Not encrypted, half duplex, no acks. Untested on real OpenMANET gear.
PTT toggle mode (tap once to talk, tap again to stop)
VOX (voice activated, 3 s pre-roll, 5 s hang)
Press the USB PTT button or key now…
Microphone permission is needed to transmit.
No sheets yet. Tap Generate to make some, or Import ones shared with you.
Modern DRYAD special symbols (shuffled in with A–Z)
Secure random, then share the sheets (normal use)
Emergency only: rebuild from a phrase

Emergency only. Phrase sheets are only as strong as the phrase: anyone who guesses it can rebuild every sheet. Use them only when you cannot share real sheets, and replace them with random sheets as soon as you can.
Channel names (each name is the passcode)
Changes to your callsign, channel names or network apply straight away: the radio re-joins when you go back.
Speak an announcement when a map point (POI) arrives
Swap "who sent what, when" with the channel, so a phone that was briefly off air catches up
Only a short list goes out (sender, type, time), never pictures. Missed messages, reports and map points are then fetched; missed pictures and files show in Chat so you can ask for them again.
Lost-device protection: erase all app data after 2 wrong PIN entries

Needs a PIN. Erases only this app\'s own data on this phone: channel names and keys, settings, PIN, chat and report history, map points, DRYAD sheets, received files and offline map tiles in the app folder. Nothing is sent on air and nothing else on the phone is touched. The app then closes and starts fresh.
Quick map point at my position
About this app (how it was made, and the prompt to build your own)
Public channel key (everyone with the same key shares Public; not private)
Show the Public channel on the home screen
Show the OpenMANET* channel on the home screen
Share these settings and DRYAD sheets with the channel…
Use a connected Bluetooth headset for radio audio and microphone (e.g. FalconClaw)
Phone setup QR code (for new phones)
Call button: rings everyone on the channel; ring when someone calls (phone ringer, plus speaker / Bluetooth / headphones)
Radio silent (receive only): nothing is sent, not voice, messages, positions, acks or map tiles
Send my location when I transmit (and every 30 s while I keep talking)
Acknowledgement mode (range test / debug): reply \"ACK\" to every message and report received, with when it was sent and how long it took. Acks are never acked.
Radio: big PTT and quick buttons
Map: mostly map and POIs, smaller PTT and shortcuts (long-press the map to drop a POI)
Also listen to a second channel: the other of A/B, or Public (choose it on the Channels page). Listen only: you only ever talk on the channel selected.
Quiet: both ears, the other channel a little quieter
Stereo: A in the left ear, B in the right (use headphones)
Save the other channel\'s voice as recordings in Chat; its messages and reports go to Chat too
Take a photo and send it
Permissions and running in the background…
When the app starts, rejoin the channel it was on (with dual watch, that channel stays the main one)
Volume all the way down = stealth: nothing plays and nothing rings; what arrives is saved in Chat and you show red to others
In stealth or with the volume at zero, vibrate for messages, voice and calls
With the volume all the way down, a received Call turns the speaker and ringer back up and rings
Possible gunshots alert* (untested): 3 very loud bangs within 10 s send \"possible gunshots\" with your position to the channel
Record all voice, sent and received (even when Available)
Every transmission on the channels you are on is saved to Chat as a recording, including your own. About 1 MB a minute: use Clear mission data to remove them.

Missed messages and voice: each channel has a \"Request catch-ups\" tick on the Channels page (on for your channels, off for Public). Coming back to the app then asks the others at once for what was sent meanwhile, shown unread in Chat.
Commander view: when someone comes back after being offline, offer for 10 s to send them what they missed
Channel settings (names, Public, dual watch, catch-up)…
Home screen (style, map points, black screen, TV)…
Network and sync (WiFi, tunnel, LAN storage, ATAK)…
Mission and data (mission, fake GPS, clearing data)…
Show a Black screen button on the home screen

Black screen covers the whole screen in black with the backlight at its lowest, while the app stays on air. To get out of it: DOUBLE-TAP the screen. Hardware and Bluetooth PTT buttons keep working while it is black. The menu also has Blackout screen.
Start tone: a short beep at the start of each PTT transmission so others start listening (the first 0.16 s of your voice is replaced by it)
Internet audio: show Radio streams in the menu (public scanner feeds; needs internet)
Erases everything this app keeps on this phone (channels, DRYAD sheets, settings, PIN, history, map points, files, offline maps) and closes it. The next time it opens, the setup wizard starts again.
Alert me when someone on my channel drops out (not heard for 2 minutes)
Crash detection* (a hard jolt asks if you are OK; no answer in 30 s sends a rescue alert with your position). *Untested
Black screen after this many seconds without a touch on the home screen (0 = never)

Deletes chat and report history, pictures and files sent or received, voice recordings, map points and contacts\' last positions. Keeps DRYAD sheets, channel names, settings and offline maps. You must leave every channel first.
Tunnel comms: connect to a relay over the internet…
Tunnel relay: let remote phones connect to this one…

For a phone away from the group\'s WiFi. The relay (best the commander tablet) stays on the group\'s network with a port forwarded to it from the internet, one port per remote person, each keyed by its own DRYAD row. The remote phone then sends and receives everything through the relay instead of WiFi. UDP, falling back to TCP. Everything stays encrypted end to end.
* Untested. A phone microphone cannot tell a gunshot from a slammed door. Keeps the microphone open while on air (nothing is sent until it triggers) and uses more battery.
